tell: An oral prodrug of fluorouracil, with 96% of its dose recovered in urine.

clues.text: Food cuts peak concentration by 60% and exposure by 34%. Plasma protein binding is under 60%, and urine carries 96% of the radiolabeled dose.
A crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 359.35 and an aqueous solubility of 26 mg/mL at 20°C.
Approved under an NDA as 150 mg and 500 mg tablets, dosed twice daily.

Boxed warning for death in complete DPD deficiency and for bleeding with vitamin K antagonists. Contraindicated after severe hypersensitivity to the drug or a close relative; anemia and diarrhea are common.
Adjuvant treatment of stage III colon cancer, perioperative treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer, unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer, and metastatic breast cancer with docetaxel.
Converted to fluorouracil in vivo; its metabolites form a covalent ternary complex with thymidylate synthase, blocking thymidylate and so DNA synthesis.
The generic name begins with C and has twelve letters.
